title: Cap. IV Arg. 9: decree whose foundation is Christ is election itself — salvandis credentibus
latin: Arg. 9. Illud Dei de salute humana decretum cujus fundamentum est Christus, est ipsissima electio ad salutem: Decretum Dei de salvandis credentibus est illud decretum salutis cujus fundamentum est Christus: Ergo decretum de salvandis fidelibus est ipsissima electio ad salutem. Majorem dicunt esse manifestam; quia nulla est salus vel benedictio ad salutem nisi in Christo. Minorem aeque perspicuam asserunt; quandoquidem illud unicum decretum est fundamentum Christianismi, salutis, et certitudinis de salute: Christianismi; quia eo constituitur Christus a Deo Salvator et Caput eorum qui participes salutis futuri sunt: Salutis; quia hoc est decretum εὐδοκίας sive beneplaciti Dei in Christo, cui tota salus nostra innititur: Certitudinis de salute; quandoquidem certitudo nostra omnis huic fulcro innixa est; Credentes salvabuntur: Ego credo: Ergo Ego salvabor.
pass_a: Argument 9. That decree of God concerning human salvation whose foundation is Christ is the very election itself to salvation: The decree of God concerning those to be saved who believe is that decree of salvation whose foundation is Christ: Therefore the decree concerning the faithful to be saved is the very election itself to salvation. They say the Major is manifest; because there is no salvation or blessing unto salvation except in Christ. They assert the Minor equally clear; seeing that that only decree is the foundation of Christianity, of salvation, and of certainty concerning salvation: of Christianity; because by it Christ is constituted by God Savior and Head of those who will be partakers of salvation: of Salvation; because this is the decree of good pleasure of God in Christ, on which our whole salvation rests: of Certainty concerning salvation; seeing that all our certainty rests on this prop; Believers will be saved: I believe: Therefore I will be saved.
pass_b: Arg. 9. God's decree on human salvation whose foundation is Christ is election itself to salvation. The decree to save believers is that salvation-decree founded on Christ. Therefore the decree to save the faithful is election itself. They call the Major plain — no salvation or blessing unto salvation except in Christ. The Minor equally clear: that one decree is the foundation of Christianity, of salvation, and of certainty of salvation — Christianity, because by it God constitutes Christ Savior and Head of those who will share salvation; salvation, because it is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ on which our whole salvation rests; certainty, because all our assurance rests on this prop: Believers will be saved; I believe; therefore I will be saved.

lemmas.gloss: Christ the foundation of the decree

title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol: owed conclusion is foresight-election; Major imperfect if made universal
latin: Sol. Observandum est, in nullo argumento Remonstrantium debitam conclusionem prodire. Nam aliud est concludere, Ergo decretum de salvandis credentibus est ipsissima electio ad salutem; aliud, Ergo Electio ipsissima ad salutem fit ex praevisione fidei antecedaneae. Hanc conclusionem frustra exspectavimus, quae nusquam visa est comparere. Sed rationem praedictam, qualem qualem, discutiamus. Major imperfecte admodum explicat rationem Electionis; nec vera est usquequaque, si universaliter intelligatur, sicuti oportet, nisi syllogismum vaders velimus nobis obtrudere. Fiat ergo universalis, hoc modo, Omne Dei de salute humana decretum cujus fundamentum est Christus, est ipsissima singularium personarum electio ad salutem. Attexatur Minor, At decretum de salvandis credentibus (id est, quibuslibet hominibus, si credant) est illud decretum salutis cujus fundamentum est Christus: Ergo hoc decretum de salvandis Credentibus est ipsissima singularium personarum electio ad salutem.
pass_a: Solution. It is to be observed that in no argument of the Remonstrants does the owed conclusion come forth. For it is one thing to conclude, Therefore the decree concerning believers to be saved is the very election itself to salvation; another, Therefore the very election itself to salvation is made from foresight of antecedent faith. This conclusion we have waited for in vain, which has nowhere been seen to appear. But let us discuss the aforesaid reason, such as it is. The Major explains the reason of Election quite imperfectly; nor is it true throughout, if it be understood universally, as it ought, unless we wish a slippery syllogism to be thrust upon us. Let it therefore be made universal, in this way: Every decree of God concerning human salvation whose foundation is Christ is the very election itself of singular persons to salvation. Let the Minor be attached, But the decree concerning believers to be saved (that is, any men whatsoever, if they believe) is that decree of salvation whose foundation is Christ: Therefore this decree concerning Believers to be saved is the very election itself of singular persons to salvation.
pass_b: Sol. Notice: in no Remonstrant argument does the owed conclusion appear. One thing is to conclude that the decree to save believers is election itself; another, that election itself is from foresight of antecedent faith — the conclusion we waited for in vain and never saw. Discuss their reason as it stands. The Major explains election quite imperfectly, and is not true throughout if taken universally as it must be, unless we let a slippery syllogism be forced on us. Make it universal: every divine decree on human salvation whose foundation is Christ is election itself of singular persons to salvation. Attach the Minor: the decree to save believers (any men, if they believe) is that Christ-founded salvation decree. Therefore that decree is election itself of singular persons.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol: diverse Christ-founded decrees — conditional gospel vs singular election
latin: Ut detegantur errores hujus argumentationis, sciendum, diversa decreta de salute humana in considerationem nostram venire posse, quorum omnium fundamentum est Christus, et tamen in illis omnibus ipsissima Electio non consistit. Sunt primo decreta nota et omnibus promulgata, quae exprimunt et continent, quibus conditionibus, vel quibus modis et mediis homines sunt ad salutem perducendi — qualia sunt, Ego salvabo omnes qui resipiscent, qui credent in Messiam, qui in hac fide et vitae novitate ad extremum usque perseverabunt. Talibus decretis omnes mortales promiscue edocentur, quibus conditionibus impletis liceat illis salutem exspectare. At iisdem nullae singulares personae ad salutem prae aliis a Deo ponuntur electae aut praedestinatae. Illorum decretorum Christus est fundamentum: quia Deus nunquam dignatus fuisset cum homine corrupto et rebelli sub talibus conditionibus agere, aut vitam aeternam credenti et resipiscenti promittere, nisi interveniente hoc novi foederis Mediatore in quo omnes promissiones Dei sunt Etiam et Amen. In hisce tamen decretis ratio electionis non includitur: quia positis talibus decretis, quae vitam omnibus peccatoribus promiscue offerunt, si crediderint et resipuerint, nisi etiam accederet aliud purae misericordiae decretum, nemo servaretur, quia nemo crederet.
pass_a: That the errors of this argumentation may be uncovered, it is to be known that diverse decrees concerning human salvation can come into our consideration, of all of which the foundation is Christ, and yet in all of them the very Election itself does not consist. There are first known decrees promulgated to all, which express and contain under what conditions, or by what modes and means, men are to be led through to salvation — such as, I will save all who repent, who will believe in the Messiah, who will persevere in this faith and newness of life even to the end. By such decrees all mortals promiscuously are taught under what conditions fulfilled it is lawful for them to expect salvation. But by the same no singular persons are set by God as elected or predestinated to salvation before others. Of those decrees Christ is the foundation: because God would never have deigned to deal with corrupt and rebellious man under such conditions, or to promise eternal life to the believing and repenting, unless with this Mediator of the new covenant intervening in whom all the promises of God are Yea and Amen. Yet in these decrees the reason of election is not included: because such decrees being posited, which offer life promiscuously to all sinners if they shall have believed and repented, unless there also came another decree of pure mercy, no one would be saved, because no one would believe.
pass_b: To expose the errors: diverse decrees on human salvation can come into view, all founded on Christ, yet election itself does not consist in all of them. First are known decrees published to all, stating under what conditions or by what means men are led to salvation — I will save all who repent, believe in the Messiah, and persevere in that faith and newness of life to the end. By those, all mortals are taught what conditions let them expect salvation. But they set no singular persons elected or predestinated before others. Christ is their foundation: God would never have deigned to deal with corrupt rebellious man under such terms, or promise eternal life to the believing and repenting, without this new-covenant Mediator in whom all God's promises are Yea and Amen. Yet election's reason is not in them: with life offered promiscuously to all sinners if they believe and repent, unless another decree of pure mercy also came, no one would be saved, because no one would believe.

lemmas.gloss: further decree of pure mercy needed

title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol: second and third decrees — singular persons and efficacious means; Major false twice
latin: Secundo, est aliud genus decretorum quo in mente et voluntate Divina ab aeterno designantur singulares personae ad salutem infallibiliter perducendae. Non nominantur quidem ipsa individua in libro Scripturae; sed inscribuntur tamen ipsa individua in libro vitae, Phil. iv. 3. Luc. x. 20. De hisce intelliguntur illa Scripturarum loca, Deus novit suos, 2 Tim. ii. 19. Ille vocat oves suas nominatim, Joan. x. 3. Ego novi quos elegerim, Joan. xiii. 18. Tertio, est cum praedicto de personis decreto colligatum semper et connexum decretum donandi singularibus illis personis omnia gratiae efficacis media, per quae ad salutem perducantur. Huc spectat illud Apostoli, Rom. viii. 30. Quos praedestinavit, vocavit; et quos vocavit, justificavit, &c. Et Ephes. i. 3–4. Benedixit nobis Deus omni benedictione spirituali, sicut elegit nos antequam jacerentur mundi fundamenta. Electio ante tempora saecularia est quasi mensura omnium spiritualium benedictionum (puta fidei, sanctitatis, perseverantiae) quae dantur in tempore; non vice versa (ut volunt Remonstrantes) praevisa fides et perseverantia, mensura electionis. Haec etiam decreta, juxta quae personae singulares ad vitam praedestinantur, et iisdem gratia salutifera praeparatur, habent Christum pro fundamento. In eo enim eliguntur tanquam membra Christo Capiti suo tempore unienda; ac per et propter eum gratia speciali hae singulares personae imbuuntur. Major itaque propositio duobus nominibus falsa est et rejicienda. Primo, quod supponit Christum solummodo fundamentum esse decreti illius universalis, Omnes credentes salvabo; cum etiam fundamentum sit hujus singularis decreti, Ego Petro, Paulo, et sic de singulis electis, vitam aeternam dabo: Ego illis singulis fidem, perseverantiam, uno verbo, gratiam ad salutem efficaciter perducentem, dabo. Secundo, falsa est Major, quod electionem in illo universali decreto formaliter constitutam supponit, cum ea se exserat in secundo decreto quo personae singulares ad vitam eliguntur, et in tertio, quo ad media efficacia prae aliis participanda destinantur, juxta celebrem apud Theologos praedestinationis definitionem, praedestinatio est praeparatio gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro.
pass_a: Secondly, there is another kind of decrees by which in the Divine mind and will from eternity singular persons are designated to be led through infallibly to salvation. The very individuals are indeed not named in the book of Scripture; but yet the very individuals are inscribed in the book of life, Phil. 4:3; Luke 10:20. Of these those places of the Scriptures are understood, God knows his own, 2 Tim. 2:19. He calls his sheep by name, John 10:3. I know whom I have chosen, John 13:18. Thirdly, there is always bound and connected with the aforesaid decree concerning persons a decree of gifting to those singular persons all the means of efficacious grace by which they may be led through to salvation. Hither looks that of the Apostle, Rom. 8:30. Whom he predestinated, he called; and whom he called, he justified, &c. And Ephes. 1:3–4. God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing, even as he chose us before the foundations of the world were laid. Election before the ages of the world is as it were the measure of all spiritual blessings (for example of faith, holiness, perseverance) which are given in time; not the other way round (as the Remonstrants will) foresight faith and perseverance, the measure of election. These decrees also, according to which singular persons are predestinated to life, and saving grace is prepared for the same, have Christ for foundation. For in him they are elected as members to be united in their time to Christ their Head; and through and on account of him these singular persons are imbued with special grace. The Major proposition therefore is false on two counts and to be rejected. First, that it supposes Christ to be the foundation only of that universal decree, I will save all believers; whereas he is also the foundation of this singular decree, I will give eternal life to Peter, to Paul, and so of each of the elect: I will give to those individuals faith, perseverance, in a word, grace efficaciously leading through to salvation. Secondly, the Major is false, that it suppose election formally constituted in that universal decree, whereas it puts itself forth in the second decree by which singular persons are elected to life, and in the third, by which they are destined to share efficacious means before others, according to the celebrated definition of predestination among Theologians, predestination is the preparation of grace in the present, and of glory in the future.
pass_b: Second: another kind of decrees by which from eternity singular persons are designated in God's mind and will to be led infallibly to salvation. The individuals are not named in Scripture's book, yet they are written in the book of life (Phil. 4:3; Luke 10:20). Of these: God knows his own (2 Tim. 2:19); he calls his sheep by name (John 10:3); I know whom I have chosen (John 13:18). Third: always bound to that person-decree is a decree to gift those singular persons every means of efficacious grace by which they are led to salvation. So Rom. 8:30 — whom he predestinated he called, whom he called he justified — and Eph. 1:3–4. Election before the ages is as it were the measure of all spiritual blessings given in time (faith, holiness, perseverance); not the reverse, as Remonstrants will, foresight faith and perseverance measuring election. These decrees too have Christ for foundation: in him they are elected as members to be united in time to Christ their Head, and through and for him they are imbued with special grace. So the Major is false twice: it makes Christ foundation only of I will save all believers, when he is also foundation of I will give eternal life to Peter, Paul, and each elect — faith, perseverance, grace leading effectively to salvation. And it locates election formally in that universal decree, whereas election puts itself forth in the second decree electing singular persons to life and the third destinating them to efficacious means before others — per the theologians' definition: predestination is preparation of grace now and glory hereafter.

lemmas.gloss: singular persons in book of life

title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol: Minor — Christ founds more than the general decree; Christianity's true foundations
latin: Ad Minorem verbo respondere sufficit; Christum esse fundamentum generalis ejus decreti de salvandis quibuscunque sub conditione fidei; sed non ejus solius, verum etiam aliorum decretorum, secundum quae singularibus personis, Christo a Patre datis ante jacta mundi fundamenta, gratia et gloria suo tempore donabitur. Non debuerunt Remonstrantes tam obstinato silentio obruere haec posteriora decreta, et in illo primo universali haerere, nisi opinentur nullum unquam fuisse decretum in mente Divina de singularibus personis efficaci gratia imbuendis, et per talem gratiam ad gloriam perducendis. Pergamus, et ea pensitemus quae ad confirmationem utriusque propositionis adducta sunt. Majorem clamant esse manifestam, quia nulla est salus vel benedictio ad salutem nisi in Christo. Frivola probatio. An quia nullum beneficium decernitur in nos conferendum nisi in Christo, idcirco quodlibet decretum ad salutem nostram spectans, cujus fundamentum est Christus, erit ipsissima nostra electio? Tam hoc cohaeret quam arena sine calce. Sed Minorem perspicuam etiam esse dicunt, quia illud unicum decretum, Ego salvabo omnes Credentes, est fundamentum Christianismi, salutis, et certitudinis de salute. Respondeo, illud unicum decretum generale non esse fundamentum Christianismi. Sunt enim alia Christianismi fundamenta, et inter alia illud praecipuum fundamentum; Fidem et perseverantiam, ac quicquid ad caelum ducit infallibiliter, esse specialia specialis gratiae dona, non autem contingentia effecta ex arbitrio hominis nondum electi nascentia, et electionis Divinae motiva.
pass_a: To answer the Minor in a word suffices; that Christ is the foundation of that general decree concerning whosoever are to be saved under the condition of faith; but not of that alone, but also of other decrees, according to which to singular persons, given by the Father to Christ before the foundations of the world were laid, grace and glory will be gifted in their time. The Remonstrants ought not to have buried these latter decrees under such obstinate silence, and to stick in that first universal one, unless they opine that there never was any decree in the Divine mind concerning singular persons to be imbued with efficacious grace, and by such grace to be led through to glory. Let us go on, and weigh those things which have been brought forward for confirmation of either proposition. They cry that the Major is manifest, because there is no salvation or blessing unto salvation except in Christ. A frivolous proof. Is it because no benefit is decreed to be conferred on us except in Christ, that therefore any decree whatsoever looking to our salvation, whose foundation is Christ, will be our very election itself? This coheres as sand without lime. But they say the Minor also is clear, because that only decree, I will save all Believers, is the foundation of Christianity, of salvation, and of certainty concerning salvation. I answer, that that only general decree is not the foundation of Christianity. For there are other foundations of Christianity, and among others that chief foundation; that Faith and perseverance, and whatever leads infallibly to heaven, are special gifts of special grace, not contingent effects arising from the choice of a man not yet elected, and motives of Divine election.
pass_b: On the Minor in a word: Christ is foundation of that general decree to save whosoever under the condition of faith — but not of that alone; also of other decrees by which singular persons, given by the Father to Christ before the world's foundations, will in their time be gifted grace and glory. Remonstrants should not bury those later decrees in obstinate silence and stick in the first universal one, unless they think there never was a decree in God's mind to imbue singular persons with efficacious grace and lead them by it to glory. They cry the Major plain because no salvation except in Christ — a frivolous proof. Because no benefit is decreed for us except in Christ, is every Christ-founded salvation-decree therefore our election itself? That coheres like sand without lime. They say the Minor is clear because I will save all Believers founds Christianity, salvation, and certainty. I answer: that general decree alone is not Christianity's foundation. There are others — chief among them that faith, perseverance, and whatever leads infallibly to heaven are special gifts of special grace, not contingent effects from the choice of a man not yet elected, and motives of divine election.

lemmas.gloss: Christ founds more than the general decree

title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol close: general decree not sufficient certainty; Cap. IV Collocutors' args end
latin: Porro, hoc fundamentum quod nos asserimus, multo magis probat Christum a Deo constitutum Salvatorem et Caput eorum qui servabuntur, quam illud generale quod ab istis urgetur. Nam in illo, Omnes qui credent salvabuntur, pactum salutis cum humano genere initum ostenditur propter Christum; sed quod effectu carebit nisi conditio credendi a nobis impleatur; qua de re in illo decreto nihil constitutum est. At quando defendimus, Deum insuper decrevisse propter Christum dare gratiam fidem et vitam omnibus electis, et ex plenitudine ejus realiter in eos diffundere hanc gratiam efficacem et salutiferam: non nudo pacto, sed ipso facto facimus Christum Salvatorem, et Caput eorum omnium qui fiunt salutis participes. Adhaec illud generale decretum, Omnes credentes salvabuntur, non est decretum illud εὐδοκίας cui tota salus nostra innititur. Nam hoc decretum est, ut sic dicam, declarativum et doctrinale; sed salus singularium personarum niti debet decreto Dei practico et operante. Misere ageretur nobiscum, si tota nostra salus niteretur hoc pacto conditionato, Si credideris salvus eris, et non esset aliud εὐδοκίας Divinae decretum de fide nobis danda, nobisque efficaciter servandis. Denique illud generale decretum, Omnes credentes salvabuntur, non potest esse alicui personae singulari fundamentum sufficiens certitudinis de salute sua. Nam illud decretum neminem servat sua sola virtute: Imo multi damnabuntur qui sciunt et credunt omnes credentes et resipiscentes fore salvandos. Accedat ergo oportet ad certitudinem faciendam alterius decreti efficacia; Nimirum, quod ego credam, quod ego in finem usque perseverabо. At unde haec certitudo fidei meae, et perseverantiae meae? Non a contingente meo libero arbitrio; ergo ab immutabili aliquo decreto Divino. Si igitur rem spectemus, certitudo salutis quoad hanc vel illam personam singularem niti debet decreto aliquo Dei practico infallibiliter decernente et operante salutem ejusdem. Si certam rei cognitionem quoad nos: certitudo salutis nostrae niti debet revelatione aliqua ejusdem decreti, per Spiritum adoptionis, et effecta ejusdem in cordibus singulorum. Nam Spiritus ille testificatur spiritui nostro nos esse illos Dei filios, quos destinavit aeternae vitae, quosque sanctificavit in hoc saeculo, ut possit glorificare in futuro. Caeterum in illo universali decreto per modum legis promulgato, Quisquis crediderit salvus erit, nec certa salus cujusquam singularis personae fundari potest, nec certa cognitio cujusquam de salute sua infallibiliter futura. Atque haec sunt omnia illa argumenta, quibus Collocutores conati sunt stabilire electionem hominum singularium ex antecedanea fidei praevisae conditione. Quae omnia ex Arminii scriptis desumpta sunt.
pass_a: Further, this foundation which we assert much more proves Christ constituted by God Savior and Head of those who will be saved, than that general one which is urged by these. For in that, All who will believe will be saved, a pact of salvation entered with the human race is shown on account of Christ; but which will lack effect unless the condition of believing is fulfilled by us; concerning which matter nothing is constituted in that decree. But when we defend that God has further decreed on account of Christ to give grace, faith, and life to all the elect, and from his fullness really to pour out into them this efficacious and saving grace: not by a bare pact, but by the very fact we make Christ Savior, and Head of all those who become partakers of salvation. Besides, that general decree, All believers will be saved, is not that decree of good pleasure on which our whole salvation rests. For this decree is, so to speak, declarative and doctrinal; but the salvation of singular persons ought to rest on a practical and operating decree of God. It would go miserably with us, if our whole salvation rested on this conditioned pact, If you shall have believed you will be saved, and there were not another decree of Divine good pleasure concerning faith to be given to us, and us to be efficaciously saved. Finally that general decree, All believers will be saved, cannot be for any singular person a sufficient foundation of certainty concerning his salvation. For that decree saves no one by its own virtue alone: Nay many will be damned who know and believe that all believers and repenting will be saved. There ought therefore to come for making certainty the efficacy of another decree; Namely, that I believe, that I will persevere even to the end. But whence this certainty of my faith, and of my perseverance? Not from my contingent free choice; therefore from some immutable Divine decree. If therefore we look at the thing, certainty of salvation as to this or that singular person ought to rest on some practical decree of God infallibly decreeing and operating the salvation of the same. If certain knowledge of the thing as to us: certainty of our salvation ought to rest on some revelation of the same decree, through the Spirit of adoption, and the effects of the same in the hearts of individuals. For that Spirit witnesses to our spirit that we are those sons of God, whom he destined to eternal life, and whom he has sanctified in this age, that he may glorify in the future. For the rest, in that universal decree promulgated after the manner of a law, Whoever shall have believed will be saved, neither can the certain salvation of any singular person be founded, nor anyone's certain knowledge of his salvation infallibly future. And these are all those arguments by which the Collocutors tried to establish the election of singular men from the antecedent condition of foresight faith. All of which have been taken from the writings of Arminius.
pass_b: Further: the foundation we assert proves far more that God constituted Christ Savior and Head of those who will be saved than their general one. All who will believe will be saved shows a pact of salvation with the human race for Christ's sake — but it lacks effect unless we fulfill the believing condition, about which that decree constitutes nothing. When we defend that God further decreed for Christ's sake to give grace, faith, and life to all the elect, and from his fullness really pour efficacious saving grace into them, we make Christ Savior and Head of all who share salvation not by bare pact but by the fact itself. Besides, All believers will be saved is not the good-pleasure decree our whole salvation rests on — it is, so to speak, declarative and doctrinal; singular persons' salvation must rest on a practical operating decree of God. It would go miserably with us if all our salvation rested on If you believe you will be saved, with no further good-pleasure decree to give us faith and save us efficaciously. Finally that general decree cannot be any singular person's sufficient certainty of his salvation: it saves no one by its own virtue alone — many will be damned who know and believe all believers and repenting will be saved. Certainty needs another decree's efficacy: that I believe, that I will persevere to the end. Whence that certainty of my faith and perseverance? Not from my contingent free choice — therefore from some immutable divine decree. As to the thing: certainty for this or that singular person rests on a practical decree infallibly decreeing and working that person's salvation. As to our knowledge: certainty rests on some revelation of that decree through the Spirit of adoption and its effects in individuals' hearts — that Spirit witnesses to our spirit that we are those sons of God destined to eternal life, sanctified in this age to be glorified hereafter. In the universal law-form decree Whoever believes will be saved, neither certain salvation of any singular person nor certain knowledge of one's infallibly future salvation can be founded. And these are all the Collocutors' arguments trying to establish election of singular men from the antecedent condition of foresight faith — all taken from Arminius's writings.
